carousels.caption:
ChatGPT’s free plan trains on everything you paste—unless you flip this switch. 
Most users don’t know their data is being stored. Here’s how to opt out in 30 seconds. 
#aiforbusiness #aitoolsforbusiness #marketingaudit #irishbusiness
carousels.hook: ChatGPT’s free plan trains on your pasted data
carousels.throughline: ChatGPT’s free plan uses your pasted data to train its AI—here’s how to stop it and keep your business info private.

reel_beats.hook: ChatGPT’s free plan trains on your pasted data

body.text: Open settings, click ‘Data controls,’ and you’ll see a toggle called ‘Improve the model for everyone.’
It’s on by default, which means every chat, customer detail, or ad copy you paste is stored.
Turning it off stops your business data from being used to train future AI versions.
Paid plans don’t train on your data, but free users must opt out manually—check it now.

screen.title: Flip this switch to stop training
options: Do not train on my data
screen.mechanism: Turning this off stops ChatGPT from using your pasted data to train its AI.

body_slides.text: Open ChatGPT settings → click ‘Data controls’ → find ‘Improve the model for everyone’
This toggle is on by default—it lets ChatGPT use your chats to train future AI
Turning it off stops your business data, customer details, or ad copy from being stored
Paid plans don’t train on your data, but free users must opt out manually
Even one paste with customer info can be used if the toggle stays on
Check this setting every few weeks—updates sometimes reset it

carousels.throughline: Google Ads mislabels 20% of buyers as low intent—here’s how to find and convert them.

reel_beats.hook: Google Ads mislabels 1 in 5 buyers as low intent

body.text: Open the Search terms report and filter for ‘Low intent’ conversions—these are buyers Google got wrong.
Some convert at 12%, not 0%, but most accounts ignore them because they’re buried in ‘Other searches.’

Run this check weekly—Google updates labels every few days, so yesterday’s ‘low intent’ might be today’s buyer.

carousels.caption:
Gmail moves your email to Primary after one reply—here’s how to get more. 
Opens don’t matter as much as replies. This checklist helps you trigger them. 
#emailmarketingtips #emaildeliverability #conversiontracking #galwaybusiness
carousels.hook: Gmail moves your email to Primary after one reply
carousels.throughline: Gmail moves emails to Primary after one reply—here’s how to trigger replies and boost inbox placement.

reel_beats.hook: Gmail moves your email to Primary after one reply

body.text: Ask a question in the first line—‘What’s your biggest challenge with X?’—to spark replies instantly.
Short subject lines (under 6 words) get more replies than long, clever ones.
Add a P.S. with a clear call to action—‘Hit reply and tell me your thoughts’—to boost engagement.
Send from a real person’s name, not ‘noreply@’—replies go to Primary faster and stay there.

screen.title: Trigger replies to reach Primary
screen.mechanism: Sending from a real name increases replies and inbox placement.

reel_beats.send_line: Send this to your email team

body_slides.text: Ask a question in the first line: ‘What’s your biggest challenge with X?’
Keep subject lines under 6 words to boost reply rates
Add a P.S. with a clear call to action: ‘Hit reply and tell me your thoughts’
Send from a real person’s name, not ‘noreply@’—replies go to Primary faster
Follow up within 24 hours if no reply—Gmail notices quick engagement
Aim for 3-5% reply rates to see a lift in inbox placement

carousels.caption:
Gmail ignores ‘free’ if your sender score is 90+—here’s how to keep it that way. 
Spammy words don’t matter if your score is strong. This myth-buster shows you how. 
#emailmarketingtips #emaildeliverability #marketingbudget #dublinbusiness
carousels.hook: Gmail ignores ‘free’ if your sender score is 90+
carousels.throughline: Gmail ignores ‘free’ in subject lines if your sender score is high—here’s how to keep it high and avoid spam filters.

reel_beats.hook: Gmail ignores ‘free’ if your sender score is 90+

body.text: Your sender score is a number (0-100) that Gmail uses to judge your emails—aim for 90+.
A high score lets you use ‘free,’ ‘discount,’ or ‘limited time’ without getting flagged.
Low scores (under 70) get sent to spam even without spammy words—check yours at senderscore.org.
Warm up new domains for 4-6 weeks before sending bulk emails to keep your score high.

screen.title: Sender score trumps spammy words
screen.mechanism: A high sender score lets you use words like ‘free’ without being flagged.

reel_beats.send_line: Send this to your email marketer

Check your score for free at senderscore.org—it updates weekly

Clean your list every 3 months—remove unengaged subscribers
